assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to degradation-resistant agonists, opened a new class of therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large effects on body weight and cardiometabolic outcomes. The mechanistic chain from hormone biology to a transformative drug class is unusually clear and of lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of the native peptide), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2 and translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form and its synthesis) form a defensible trio. Knudsen (drug design at the company) is credited but is arguably industrial development; Habener is not in the supplied names, so credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and very large phase 3 and outcome trials; the clinical impact is now broad and undeniable, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the identification of the active GLP-1 peptide are unresolved on my reading.
Whether the committee wants to credit the drug-development step (Knudsen) in place of a basic-science laureate.
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, millisecond control of genetically defined cells using microbial opsins. It is a general-purpose method that has transformed circuit analysis, and it has now reached early clinical use in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the main difficulty. Nagel and Hegemann (and Bamberg) established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck demonstrated neuronal control. A trio of Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann is one plausible configuration, but the exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for over fifteen years and a standard laboratory tool; mature and extensively validated.
uncertainties: Six credited people against a three-laureate limit; any configuration omits someone with a strong claim.
Methods versus discovery: the prize may be argued to favour a tool rather than a biological finding.
Extent of clinical impact is still small.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered chimeric antigen receptor T cells created a new cancer treatment modality, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now expansion toward myeloma and autoimmune disease. This is a clear conceptual and clinical advance in medicine.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR with costimulation) and June (clinical translation, first successful trials) are central. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early CAR clinical work; Eshhar and others are not in the supplied names, so the credit list may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of long-term follow-up; timely, though solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity management remain unsettled.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR concept credit (not in supplied names) is not represented.
Rosenberg versus other adoptive-therapy contributors in a three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined an entirely new intracellular signalling pathway from the ER to the nucleus (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing), explaining how cells sense and respond to protein-folding stress. It is a conceptually original discovery with wide relevance to physiology and disease.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently identified the signalling components in yeast and mammals; this is a clean, two-person configuration and the supplied credit supports it.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of independent confirmation; the core pathway is stable, with translational payoff in disease still developing.
uncertainties: Direct clinical impact is less established than for therapy-led candidates.
Contributions of others, such as the PERK/eIF2alpha arm, are not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one. The work links basic RNA splicing mechanism to a clear therapeutic proof of principle for antisense medicines.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing regulatory elements and the ASO strategy; Bennett drove antisense chemistry and development. The supplied pair is coherent, although the Adrian Krainer and Ionis collaboration and other groups' contributions may need weighing.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong long-term outcomes; recognition is timely, with convincing clinical confirmation.
uncertainties: Some of the credit belongs to broader antisense chemistry work not captured in the names.
Related SMN gene therapy and small molecules complicate the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are a rare case of cancer prevention at population scale, with strong evidence for reduction of cervical precancer and cancer. The impact on global health is large, and the L1 VLP concept is original and decisive.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP) and Frazer (VLP expression and vaccine development) are a plausible trio, although other groups (Zhou, Kirnbauer and others) have competing claims that are not part of the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Population-level cancer outcome data are now emerging, which strengthens maturity; the discovery is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among several groups on VLP formation.
Proximity to the 2008 HPV prize (zur Hausen) might make a second HPV award appear redundant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that chaperonins actively assist protein folding in an ATP-dependent manner resolved a central question in protein biology after Anfinsen's work, and underlies our understanding of proteostasis and misfolding disease.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl jointly established the GroEL/GroES-assisted folding in vitro and in mitochondria; the supplied two-person credit is clean.
assessment.maturity: Long-standing, well-confirmed mechanism with textbook status; arguably overdue, though direct medical relevance is indirect.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this primarily chemistry rather than physiology or medicine.
Contributions of others in the chaperone field (for example Ellis, Georgopoulos) are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and of its role in nutrient-dependent growth control placed a central regulator at the heart of cell growth, metabolism, ageing and cancer, with clinical use of rapalogs.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its function; Schreiber contributed the rapamycin/FKBP12 chemical biology and the mammalian target purification. Sabatini's contribution to mTORC1 nutrient sensing is credited but not selected here, partly because of unresolved concerns about his standing; I treat the allocation as unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and highly cited; clinical benefit exists but is modest compared with the biological importance.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and others in the earlier rapamycin work is unresolved.
Therapeutic payoff of mTOR inhibition has been smaller than anticipated.
